eventPolicy.costRule: Keep paid events and record cost/registration fields when visible.
eventPolicy.sourceUrlRule: Every event must keep the original event page or source calendar URL.
eventPolicy.qualityRule: Every import must check date coverage, time, place, coordinates, source URL, and activity summary before writing events.json; summaries must contain only useful activity content, not date, time, venue, room, place, or address text; automatically repair deterministic gaps and report anything still missing.
eventPolicy.dateRangeRule: When an event is listed as a date range, expand it so every calendar day in the range is represented unless the source clearly describes one overnight event.
eventPolicy.allDayTimeRule: When an event is listed as all day, check official venue/source hours for that date before filling exact times; if exact hours are not confirmed, leave exact time fields blank where possible and mark timeStatus for review.
eventPolicy.missingAddressRule: When an event gives a venue but no address, search official venue/source pages first, then reliable map or directory sources for the exact street address; if still not found, leave address blank or mark approximate/needs_review rather than guessing.

requiredChecks: date range expansion so every active calendar day has a record or a review marker
startsAt, an exact time, or a clear timeLabel with timeStatus when exact time is unavailable
address when available from the source, official venue page, or reliable address reference
official page text first, then image/flyer text for address, time, room, and venue only when HTML text is incomplete
lat/lng for every in-coverage event shown on the map
summary with concrete activity content only, excluding date, time, venue, room, place, and address text
sourceUrl or url pointing back to the original event page
autoRepair: Copy url and sourceUrl from each other when one is missing.
Copy venue and venueName from each other when one is missing.
Fill timezone from eventPolicy.timezone when startsAt is present.
Calculate durationMinutes from startsAt and endsAt when possible.
Expand multi-day date ranges into per-day event records when the source indicates the event is active across the range.
For all-day rows, fill exact times only from official operating hours for the event date; otherwise preserve a timeLabel and mark timeStatus.
Look up missing venue addresses from official venue/source pages, then reliable map or directory references; do not write guessed addresses.
Use source library/location coordinates first, then town center fallback, then address geocoding for missing in-coverage lat/lng.
Clean generic source-page/update/registration filler and date/time/place/address/venue text out of summaries.
importQuality.unresolvedReportRule: If time, place, coordinates, source URL, or concrete summary are still missing after auto-repair, print an import quality audit with counts and sample event IDs/titles for manual review.
importQuality.contentRule: Do not invent activity descriptions. Extract concrete activity content from the source page when possible; if unavailable, leave summary empty and report it. Put date, time, venue, room, place, and address only in structured fields such as startsAt, endsAt, timeLabel, venueName, venue, and address, never in summary.
importQuality.imageTextRule: Always inspect official page HTML text first. Only when the page text does not provide the needed address, time, room, or venue detail should the importer inspect image alt/title/captions or OCR-visible flyer text; if the importer cannot read the image text, report the event/source for manual image review.
importQuality.uncertaintyRule: If date coverage, time, address, venue, town assignment, or summary is inferred, image-derived, approximate, missing, or uncertain, keep the event useful but mark it with status review, lower confidence, and field-level markers such as dateStatus, dateExpansionStatus, timeStatus, addressStatus, townAssignmentStatus, summaryStatus, or reviewNotes so accuracy-based QA can find it.

sourceStatusVocabulary.importable: Importer should automatically read this source and write events to data/events.json.
sourceStatusVocabulary.manual_review: Source is useful but does not have a stable importer yet; keep the link and parser notes.
sourceStatusVocabulary.service_area: Town is covered by a system source or nearby branch, but there is not a separate branch feed to import.
sourceStatusVocabulary.blocked_by_bot_protection: Source is useful but direct script fetching is blocked; keep it for future browser-backed or manual review.
sourceStatusVocabulary.reference_only: Keep as a directory, venue, or planning reference; do not import events automatically.
sourceStatusVocabulary.not_found: A source type was checked for a town and no useful dated-event source was found.
sourceStatusVocabulary.broken: A previously useful source or parser is currently failing and needs review before import.

appDisplayPolicy.townMenuRule: The More menu displays short town names without Township, Borough, or City suffixes.
appDisplayPolicy.zipRule: Single-ZIP towns show ZIP right-aligned without parentheses; multi-ZIP towns show a parent town row with indented community ZIP rows.
appDisplayPolicy.librarySearchColorRule: Towns with at least one library source marked importable are highlighted in the More menu.
appDisplayPolicy.placeNameRule: Event detail place names may be shortened for display, but source data should keep the original venue name for refresh and review.
appDisplayPolicy.placeDisplayRule: venueName should be a readable venue/place label, not only a street address, intersection, vague downtown area, route, or source placeholder. If the source gives only an address but the registry has a confirmed venue/library name, use the confirmed name for venueName and keep the address in address. If the source gives a place-like display name without a full address, such as a gazebo, bandstand, field, playground, pavilion, plaza, or named room, reverse-look up that display name with the town/venue context and use the resolved address or coordinates for navigation; mark addressLookupSource as place_name_reverse_lookup when practical. If the lookup is likely but not official, keep the useful address, mark addressStatus approximate or needs_review, and preserve the display name in venueName instead of falling back to a generic municipal default. For true street-fair, parade, downtown, route, or multi-site events, keep the broad place label only; use addressStatus area_confirmed when the area/route is confirmed but there is no single precise navigation point, otherwise use addressStatus approximate or needs_review and reviewNotes.
appDisplayPolicy.sourceLinkDisplayRule: When the same activity has multiple source pages, display only one source link in the app. Prefer an official organizer, venue, municipal, library, or program detail page. Use discovery, directory, ticketing, or reposted pages such as Patch or Eventbrite only when no official page is available. Keep extra evidence links internally when helpful for refresh or QA, but the visible button should stay a single Source page.

workflow: Add the town to towns[] with id, name, county, geoid when known, center, distanceMiles, and within-coverage status.
Find and store source links first: municipal/recreation links in towns[].municipal, library links in towns[].libraries[], and reusable or venue-specific links in sharedSources or regionalSources.

Do not stop after government and library sources. For every newly added town, complete the requiredSourceSweep across businesses, museums, arts/science venues, farms/gardens, indoor play venues, malls/retail workshops, downtown/chamber groups, county parks, and other kid-friendly places that may publish dated or limited-time events.
Mark each source with type, status from sourceStatusVocabulary, parser, website, eventsUrl, address/lat/lng when available, and notes about access or parser limits.
Run scripts/import-source-events.mjs to refresh data/events.json from importable sources while keeping older events.
Let the app read data/events.json only; events outside the 30-minute coverage can stay in JSON but should not appear in the app until they are mapped to coverage.

requiredSourceSweep.rule: Every town expansion must search beyond municipal and public-library calendars. Treat all places where children can play, learn, watch, build, craft, read, explore, or attend seasonal programs as potential event sources.
requiredSourceSweep.scope: Search sources physically in the new town plus nearby venues that serve the town or sit inside the active drive-time coverage area. Prefer official venue pages, official calendars, booking pages, and stable APIs before third-party aggregators.
minimumChecklist: Municipal calendar, parks/recreation department, recreation registration portal, municipal alliance, school/community supplement pages, and official news/flyer pages.
Public library branch calendars, county library system feeds, nearby service-area branches, and youth/teen/family pages.
Downtown/SID/chamber/business association calendars, street fairs, farmers markets, and local business district pages.
County parks, nature centers, environmental education centers, gardens, arboretums, farms, wildlife centers, zoos, and seasonal outdoor venues.
Museums, science centers, art centers, historic sites, theaters, music venues, maker spaces, and cultural centers with family or youth programs.
Indoor playgrounds, trampoline parks, sensory gyms, kids gyms, sports complexes, swim schools, dance/martial arts studios, STEM/coding centers, party venues, and camp/class providers.
Malls, shopping centers, bookstores, toy/game stores, LEGO/Apple-style retail programs, craft stores, home-improvement kids workshops, and restaurants/cafes that host family events.
Regional festival, carnival, fair, market, and tourism directories that can be mapped back to covered towns.
requiredSourceSweep.recordingRule: Record every useful source even when it is not importable yet. Use importable when an importer can read it, manual_review when it needs human/browser review, service_area when covered by a broader system, blocked_by_bot_protection when direct fetching is blocked, and reference_only only for directories or venues without dated event potential.
requiredSourceSweep.stopRule: A new town source update is incomplete until each checklist category has either an importable/manual source entry or a note explaining why no useful dated-event source was found.
